title: Private Cluster Health & Upgrade Timeline — status panel prototype
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Design a compact, at-a-glance Console panel for Private/VPC clusters that combines live health indicators, node-pool/network overlays, and a chronological upgrade timeline so SREs and platform users can quickly assess cluster state and planned maintenance. The panel should be embeddable in cluster and organization-level pages and support quick links to upgrade rollouts and incident playbooks.

Scope: initial prototype focuses on single-cluster view with ability to expand to multi-cluster list. Includes:
- Top-level health score (aggregated SLO view), current alerts count, and last successful check-in time.
- Upgrade timeline: scheduled upgrades, rolling window, step status (pending/in-progress/failed), and rollback controls.
- Networking overlay summary: VPC attachments, route table warnings, CIDR conflicts flagged as warnings.
- Node pool quick-summary: GPU/CPU counts, degraded node count, autoscale activity, and cost delta estimate for running upgrade in off-peak window.
- Live events feed with sortable filters (system/upgrade/network/security).

Design goals: clarity under stress, succinct problem-to-action flow (observe -> diagnose -> act), consistency with Redwood Console visual language, minimal cognitive load for platform engineers.
tradeoffs_and_decisions:
1) Live updates: decided to prototype with 15s polling rather than websockets to reduce infra work for the first iteration; trade-off: slightly less real-time but much easier to QA and rollback.
2) Health score calculation: prototype will surface an aggregated score with hoverable breakdown (SLOs, container restarts, node readiness). Full transparency will be part of a follow-up to avoid clutter in initial release.
3) Upgrade control surface: allow quick 'pause' and 'abort' actions from the panel, but require a confirmation modal that links to the rollout detail page. Rationale: faster mitigation path while preventing accidental interruptions.
4) Networking detail depth: surface warnings inline, but link out to a dedicated VPC topology canvas for remediation to avoid overcrowding the panel.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype artboard available in Figma with exportable states for healthy, degraded, and in-upgrade clusters
Clickable prototype demonstrates drilldown from top-level health to upgrade timeline and node pool detail
Design passes accessibility contrast checks and keyboard navigation for primary actions
PM and Eng approve interaction model for pause/abort of upgrades
Handoff tokens (colors, spacing, component props) documented in the design system page

2026-03-05 - Eng (Sofia Martinez): Concern about computation cost of live health aggregation; suggest caching health score and exposing 'refresh' control.
2026-03-07 - Security (Ravi Shah): Flag requirement to include link to audit log for upgrade approvals; noted for handoff.
2026-03-09 - UX Research (Olivia Park): Prototype testing with 5 SREs showed quick identification of failed nodes but confusion about color meaning — add legend and text labels.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Maya Chen: Initial wireframes uploaded. Focused on single-column panel to keep embedding compact. Added 'timeline compact' variant for org-level pages.

2026-03-06 - Sofia Martinez: Engineering review complete. Backend will expose /clusters/:id/health-summary and /clusters/:id/upgrades endpoints. We propose adding a 'cached_at' field to avoid repeated heavy aggregation.
2026-03-08 - Arjun Patel: Marked as high visibility for enterprise customers. Request to include cost impact estimation when scheduling upgrades during business hours.
2026-03-10 - Olivia Park: Usability test script linked in attachments; recommend adding tooltip on health score formula.
prototype_notes: Prototype uses three states: healthy (green), warning (amber), critical (red). Each upgrade step shows a micro-progress bar and estimated time remaining.
Compact timeline compresses older events into a 'history' view to reduce vertical space usage.
Mock data includes simulated CIDR conflict for testing networking warning UI and simulated node drain failures to exercise rollback flows.
risks: Overloading the panel with too many details could reduce scan-ability for on-call engineers.
Backend aggregation overhead if health score computed on every page render; mitigated by caching and 'refresh' control.
Action affordances (pause/abort) introduce safety risk—must require 2-step confirmation and audit log linkage.
